title: Add .NET RAG agent starter with tool-calling sample and docs
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Add a minimal, opinionated .NET (net7) RAG agent starter that demonstrates Redwood-compatible tool-calling, streaming responses, and a small end-to-end dev loop (local run, Docker, and GH Actions). This is intended for .NET teams who want a concise, production-sketchable example that plugs into Redwood hosted and private deployments.

What this PR adds (high level): - dotnet/rag-agent/ starter project (Minimal API) with:  - tool adapter for a simple vector DB (SQLite+ivf-lite shim) and an HTTP tool for a retrieval microservice  - prompt templates and a typed tool-calling model contract  - streaming SSE endpoint wired to Redwood API streaming with graceful reconnect logic - local dev Dockerfile and a lightweight compose file for the vector shim - GH Actions workflow for build/test and demo deploy to staging docs site - docs/quickstarts/dotnet-rag-agent.md with step-by-step, screenshots, and runbook checklist

Checklist: - [x] Minimal API implementation (Program.cs + controllers) - [x] Tool-calling contract and JSON schema for typed tools - [x] Example prompt sets and unit tests for prompt/response parsing - [x] Dockerfile and docker-compose for local emulation - [x] CI workflow added and passing - [x] Docs page with quickstart and troubleshooting

Usage summary (short): 1) dotnet restore && dotnet run in dotnet/rag-agent 2) Start the local vector shim: docker-compose up -d 3) POST to /api/ask with input JSON (see README) 4) The server will call the vector tool, build RAG context, call Redwood generation endpoint (streamed), then call an external tool (if needed) and return structured output (json with fields: answer, sources, tools_called)

Notes and motivation details: The example focuses on practical defaults: short caching TTL for vector results, explicit model pinning in appsettings.json, and a small retry/backoff wrapper around streaming connectors. This also demonstrates how to map Redwood's function/tool calling to a typed .NET contract (ToolRequest/ToolResponse) for safer integration in typed codebases.

Docs: The docs page includes a gated troubleshooting section for common issues when targeting Dedicated/Private (KMS configs, TLS cert instructions) and a small section describing how to adapt the sample to use the Redwood SDK rather than raw HTTP. Links: - Quickstart: /docs/quickstarts/dotnet-rag-agent - Example runs in GH Actions: .github/workflows/dotnet-rag-agent.yml

Migration/compatibility: No breaking changes to existing examples. This is additive to the examples corpus.
